questions.q: What is the ITIL 4 purpose of the knowledge management practice?
options: To maintain and improve the effective, efficient use of information and knowledge across the organization
To produce as much written documentation as possible for every service
To handle predefined, user-initiated requests for access or equipment
To restore normal service operation as quickly as possible after an incident
questions.explain: The purpose is about effective, efficient use of information and knowledge, not about the sheer volume of documents produced.

questions.q: In the DIKW model, what turns information into knowledge?
options: Simply storing the information in a knowledge base
Combining information with experience, so a pattern becomes recognizable and actionable
Removing all context from the raw data
Having a manager approve the information
questions.explain: Knowledge is information combined with experience — for example, recognizing that a spike in failed logins from one IP matches a known credential-stuffing pattern.

questions.q: Why does ITIL 4 favor capturing knowledge as a "byproduct" of other practices rather than as a separate documentation project?
options: Because knowledge articles are only useful if written by a dedicated documentation team
Because ITIL 4 discourages organizations from ever writing anything down
Writing it up right after resolving a major incident or a recurring question costs little extra effort while details are fresh, and produces an article the next responder can actually find
Because byproduct knowledge never needs to be reviewed or found again
questions.explain: Capturing knowledge as a byproduct of resolving an incident or answering a question keeps the effort low and the content timely, instead of letting a documentation backlog grow unused.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what is usually the real obstacle to effective knowledge management in most organizations?
options: A lack of any wiki, knowledge base, or shared drive to store information in
The DIKW model being too complex for most IT teams to apply
Knowledge management requiring specialized software that most organizations don't own
Behavior — whether people take the time to write knowledge down and whether others actually search for it before asking again
questions.explain: Most organizations already have somewhere to store knowledge; the gap is usually behavioral — capturing it and then actually searching for it before re-asking.

questions.q: A service desk agent answers the same password-reset question for the tenth time this month. What does this lesson say should happen?
options: Nothing — repeated questions don't generate any knowledge management opportunity
That answer should become a self-service knowledge article so future callers can resolve it themselves without contacting the service desk
The agent should escalate every repeat question to problem management instead of resolving it
The question should be removed from the service catalog entirely
questions.explain: A recurring question answered the same way repeatedly is exactly the kind of byproduct knowledge that should be turned into a findable article, reducing future contact volume.
